heading: Markup and styles stay in the view
body:
Write the markup of a view in its `tac.html` and its styles in its `tac.css`. A script changes text, classes and service state. It does not build markup or write styles. The build stops with `TY1364` when a JavaScript or TypeScript file under `client/` writes `innerHTML` or `outerHTML`, calls `document.write`, `insertAdjacentHTML` or `document.createElement`, inserts nodes with `append`, `appendChild`, `insertBefore` or a similar method, writes `element.style` or changes a style sheet. This covers services, component scripts and every script in `client/shared/`. It also refuses `setHTML` and `setHTMLUnsafe`, compound writes such as `innerHTML ||= html`, and these methods called through `call` or `apply`, such as `document.write.call(document, html)`. The check follows a document or a node that a variable holds, and a node kept in an object field, such as `const refs = { list: document.querySelector('#l') }`, also when another function reads the field. An object that holds only literal values is data, so `theme.style = 'light'` passes. A CSS variable is a value, not a style, so `style.setProperty('--accent', color)` and `style.removeProperty('--accent')` pass when the name is written as text that starts with `--`; a name held in a variable is refused, because the check cannot see it. The check reads the source text, so it is a guard for mistakes, not a sandbox: computed names such as `element[name]`, `Reflect.set` and `Object.assign` are not followed.

A third-party script that must build markup is a vendor file. List it in `tac.scripts` and in `tac.scriptSources` in `client/manifest.json`, with its package, exact version, license and SHA-256, and keep it in `client/shared/`, outside the utility folders. A wrong entry stops the build with `TY1365`. A file whose bytes do not match the SHA-256 stops it with `TY1403`. Tachyon publishes a vendor file unchanged.

Inline SVG works in a view. The renderer creates `<svg>` and its children in the SVG namespace, so `viewBox`, `xlink:` attributes and HTML inside `<foreignObject>` work. The example draws a cart icon inside a button.
